changes.before: Define seatCount(_ text: String) -> Int. Accept parsed integers1 through 8 inclusive; return 0 for malformed, out-of-range or otherwise rejected input.
changes.after: Leave a function early when an input cannot be used.

before: Int(text) attempts to construct an integer from text and returns Int?. It returns nil for text that cannot represent an Int, including an out-of-range integer string. It does not return zero as a general parse-failure signal. Our function deliberately chooses 0 as its own rejected-input result.

guard let number = Int(text) else requires the failure branch to exit this function. After the guard succeeds, number stays available in the remaining function body. The next guard checks the separate application range 1 through 8. Parsing and range validation answer different questions.
A booking form can reject malformed text before checking its policy. Explain which step rejects "many" and which rejects "9"; do not describe every rejected input as a parsing error.
after: `Int(text)` tries to turn text into a whole number. Its result is optional: a number on success, or nil when the text cannot fit an Int. Failure does not automatically mean zero.

`guard let number = Int(text) else` tries to get that number. The `else` part must leave the current path; here it returns 0. When the guard succeeds, `number` stays available for the rest of the function.
Reading a number and accepting it are separate checks. A whole number can still be outside the allowed range. The second guard accepts only 1 through 8, including both endpoints.
Define `seatCount(_ text: String) -> Int`. Return the accepted number. Choose 0 for every rejected input, whether conversion failed or the number was outside 1 through 8.

project.title: Leave early with guard let
project.task: Write `seatCount(_ text: String) -> Int`. Accept whole numbers from 1 through 8. Return 0 when the text cannot become an Int or the number is outside that range.
project.done_when: The checks pass for allowed values, both endpoints, unreadable text, and numbers outside the range.
